children: U.S. crude oil inventories likely saw a moderate decrease last week, while diesel stocks are seen down and gasoline stocks unchanged, according to a survey by The Wall Street Journal.

Commercial crude stocks are seen falling by 500,000 barrels to 422.9 million barrels in the week ended Sept. 18, according to the average estimate of eight analysts and traders. Six expect a decline and two predict an increase, with estimates ranging from 2.6 million barrel draw to a 1.6 million barrel build.
Gasoline inventories are seen unchanged at 207.7 million barrels, with forecasts ranging from a 1 million barrel drop to a 1.2 million barrel increase.

Stocks of distillate fuel, mostly diesel, are expected to have fallen by 500,000 barrels to 107.4 million barrels. Estimates range from a drop of 2 million barrels to an increase of 1.6 million barrels.

Refinery capacity use is seen falling by 0.6 of a percentage point to 96.2%, according to the survey. Forecasts range from a 0.1 percentage point rise to a 1 percentage point decline. One analyst didn't forecast refinery runs.
The inventory data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration is scheduled for release at 10:30 a.m. ET on Wednesday.
